correctness.rationale: At unit externality and all-zero start, each update changes a zero vertex to one exactly when no neighbor is already one; activated vertices never deactivate. Thus updates implement monotone random greedy maximal independent-set formation and stopping means the active set dominates. Star expectation is the fair coupon-collector mean m² H_(m²). For H, independent rate-1 Poisson arrivals on each of N vertices show the first biclique arrival chooses the eventually active side; its remaining m-1 side-site waits have independent Exp(1), while q=(m-1)² isolates have independent Exp(1). The completion clock is max(M_q, Exp(2m)+M_(m-1)); binomial expansion of the survival distribution and beta integration produce exactly the claimed finite sum. A Bonferroni bound yields Z_m=E[(R-I)_+]=1/m+O(m^-2), harmonic differences yield E T_G-E T_H=m-2log m+O(1). Independent exact rational recurrences for m=2,3,4,5 reproduce the beta sums, with m=2 values 25/3,33/4, gap 1/12. This proves only those tested finite instances; analytical arguments establish all m.

originality.rationale: Misiak and Dziubinski (arXiv:2602.15986v1) already exhibit the exact five-vertex cospectral pair and demonstrate differential convergence empirically; neither that pair nor qualitative non-spectral convergence is new. The surviving contribution is an exact absorbing hitting-time expectation formula for all m>=2, valid in actual individual vertex updates, and the rigorously unbounded m-2log m+O(1) difference. Terminal random greedy MIS distributions in related results do not by themselves give waiting times with repeated idle selections.

value.rationale: Exact expected convergence time quantifies decentralized public-good adjustment costs on a natural infinite cospectral pair family already motivating simulations. The rigorous gap m-2log m+O(1), though relatively vanishing, distinguishes graph spectra from the timing of equilibrium under a canonical random-with-replacement schedule. It is not merely a simulation or rediscovery of noncospectrality.

final_claim: For every m>=2, G=K_(1,m²) and H=K_(m,m) disjoint (m-1)² isolates have identical adjacency spectrum but under asynchronous uniform random unit-externality best responses from all zero, their exact mean Nash-equilibrium first-hitting times differ by m-2 log m+O(1) vertex updates; E T_G=m² H_(m²), E T_H has explicit finite beta-sum.
limitations: All-zero initial configuration, unit externality, uniformly sampled single vertex with replacement, N=m²+1.
